title.fa: حقوق زن در اسلام نخستین: ارث، محجوریت و فاصلهٔ نظر و عمل (به روایت فهمی)
title.en: Women's rights in early Islam: inheritance, legal incapacity and the gap between theory and practice (Fahmi)
title.nl: Vrouwenrechten in de vroege islam: erfrecht, handelingsonbekwaamheid en de kloof tussen theorie en praktijk (Fahmi)

summary.fa: فهمی بر آن است که قرآن در نظر برای زن حقوقی قائل شد، از جمله ارث، اما زن همچنان برابر مرد نبود و در عمل جایگاهش بعدها بدتر شد. او این را نتیجهٔ جامعهٔ پدرسالار و پدیده‌های اجتماعی بعدی می‌داند، نه محتوای قرآنی صرف.
summary.en: Fahmi argues that the Quran, in theory, gave women rights including inheritance, but without equality with men, and that in practice their position later declined. He attributes this to the patriarchal society and later social developments rather than to the Quranic text alone.
summary.nl: Fahmi stelt dat de Koran vrouwen in theorie rechten gaf, waaronder erfrecht, maar geen gelijkheid, en dat hun positie in de praktijk verslechterde door het patriarchaat en latere maatschappelijke ontwikkelingen.

text.fa: فهمی می‌گوید اسلام در جامعه‌ای مردسالار پدید آمد که قدرت پدر در آن ریشه در رسم داشت؛ با ظهور دین، این قدرت صبغهٔ الاهی گرفت و انعطاف‌ناپذیرتر شد.
text.en: Fahmi says Islam emerged in a patriarchal society where the father's authority rested on custom; with the new religion this authority took on a divine character and became less flexible.
text.nl: Fahmi says Islam emerged in a patriarchal society where the father's authority rested on custom; with the new religion this authority took on a divine character and became less flexible.

text.fa: او می‌نویسد در رسم کهن عرب زن بخشی از میراث خانوادهٔ شوهر شمرده می‌شد و از ارث بی‌بهره بود، چون ارث را نتیجهٔ مشارکت در جنگ و غنیمت می‌دانستند؛ محمد برای عواطف و خویشاوندی در ارث ملاک اخلاقی گذاشت و زن را وارث کرد.
text.en: He writes that in old Arab custom a woman could be treated as part of her husband's inheritance and had no share, since inheritance followed participation in war and booty; Muhammad introduced a moral criterion of kinship and affection and made women heirs.
text.nl: He writes that in old Arab custom a woman could be treated as part of her husband's inheritance and had no share, since inheritance followed participation in war and booty; Muhammad introduced a moral criterion of kinship and affection and made women heirs.

text.fa: به باور او نظام ارث قرآنی زن را از همهٔ محرومیت‌ها آزاد نکرد، چون سهم او نیم‌سهم مرد بود، اما این گام را پیشرفتی چشمگیر می‌داند.
text.en: In his view the Quranic inheritance system did not remove every disadvantage, since a woman received half a man's share, but he calls it a remarkable advance.
text.nl: In his view the Quranic inheritance system did not remove every disadvantage, since a woman received half a man's share, but he calls it a remarkable advance.

text.fa: فهمی تأکید می‌کند که اسلام در نظر موقعیت زن را بهتر کرد، ولی کمی بعد، زیر تأثیر پدیده‌های اجتماعی، جایگاه او در عمل نازل‌تر از دورهٔ پیش از اسلام شد؛ و می‌گوید زن عرب پیش از اسلام «شخص» بود، هرچند در نگاه امروز شیء به نظر آید.
text.en: Fahmi stresses that Islam improved women's position in theory, but soon, under social pressures, their practical standing fell below that of the pre-Islamic period; he says the pre-Islamic Arab woman was a 'person' although she may look like an object by modern standards.
text.nl: Fahmi stresses that Islam improved women's position in theory, but soon, under social pressures, their practical standing fell below that of the pre-Islamic period; he says the pre-Islamic Arab woman was a 'person' although she may look like an object by modern standards.

text.fa: این ادعا که زن پیش از اسلام آزادتر از زن پس از آن بوده، در پژوهش‌های بعدی محل بحث است: جامعهٔ پیش از اسلام ناهمگن بود (مناطق، قبیله‌ها و طبقه‌ها فرق داشتند) و منابع آن دوره عمدتاً دیرتر نوشته شده‌اند؛ بسیاری از مسلمانان و برخی پژوهشگران نیز اسلام را بهبودی در جایگاه زن می‌دانند.
text.en: The claim that pre-Islamic women were freer than later ones is debated in later scholarship: pre-Islamic society was heterogeneous (regions, tribes and classes differed) and sources for it were mostly written later; many Muslims and some scholars regard Islam as an improvement in women's status.
text.nl: The claim that pre-Islamic women were freer than later ones is debated in later scholarship: pre-Islamic society was heterogeneous (regions, tribes and classes differed) and sources for it were mostly written later; many Muslims and some scholars regard Islam as an improvement in women's status.
